newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil soars on prompt squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil soars on prompt squeeze.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps extended its early day sharp hikes into the afternoon on Thursday amid strong regional demand and scarce prompt supplies, market sources said.

January gas oil swaps was actively traded up throughout the day with deals done from $31.60 to $32.20 a barrel late this afternoon, they said. January was last quoted at $32.05/$32.20, up about 90 cents from Wednesday, they said.

Buying was also seen for the more prompt December swaps with several lots traded at $32.00 in the morning and at $32.60 and $32.90 and was latest quoted at $32.80/$33.00, up from Wednesday's $31.95/$32.15.
Traders said the market rose on strong Chinese demand for physical gas oil for delivery in December and a squeeze on December physical barrels.
The marker also firmed on expectations of increased demand from North Asia for the winter.
The jet fuel market was firm in quiet trade with prices largely unchanged from Wednesday but the jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade narrowed due to soaring gas oil prices.
January regrade was quoted at $1.55/$1.85 a barrel down about 20 cents from Wednesday, brokers said.
December fuel oil was quoted higher in line with the stronger crude market at $122.00/$123.00 a tonne, and January at $120.00/$121.00, both up about $1.00 from Wednesday.
December naphtha was also quoted firmer with bids seen at $24.60 a barrel and January quoted at $23.90/$24.10, both up about 30 cents.
